after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x=y+1 \\ x-y=2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x-y=1 \\ x-y=2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{(-1)\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now represent the solution to this system, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using an Inverse Matrix With Reorganization
content.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x=y+1 \\ x-y=2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x-y=1 \\ x-y=2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{(-1)\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now represent the solution to this system, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x-3=y \\ 3y=4x+2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x-y=3 \\ -4x+3y=2.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}].$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2\cdot 3-(-4)\cdot (-1)}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system as:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

content.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x-3=y \\ 3y=4x+2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x-y=3 \\ -4x+3y=2.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}].$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2\cdot 3-(-4)\cdot (-1)}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system as:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
